nodes.name: Corollary 1.14
nodes.statement:
Let $X$ be a projective Gorenstein variety over $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\mathsf{S}$ be a closed subspace of $\mathsf{Sing}(X)$.
   Suppose $d = \mathsf{dim}(X)$ is odd and $\mathsf{S}$ contains an \emph{isolated} singularity $s$, which is an ADE-hypersurface singularity or satisfies $\smash{\widehat{{\mathcal O}}_{X,s} \in \mathfrak{S}}$.

   If there is an algebraic categorical absorption\xspace of the singularities of $\mathsf{S}$, then $s$ is a nodal singularity, i.e.\ an $A_1$-singularity $S \cong \mathbb{C}\llbracket z_0, \ldots, z_d \rrbracket/(z_0^2 + \cdots + z_d^2 )$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.11: Cf also
nodes.statement:
Let $X$ be a projective Gorenstein variety over $\mathbb{C}$.
   Assume that $d = \mathsf{dim}(X)$ is odd and that $X$ contains an \emph{isolated} singularity $s$, which is an ADE-hypersurface singularity or satisfies $\smash{\widehat{{\mathcal O}}_{X,s} \in \mathfrak{S}}$.

  If there is an algebraic categorical absorption\xspace ${\mathcal A} = \langle \operatorname{\mathsf{D}}^{\mathrm{b}}(R_1), \dots, \operatorname{\mathsf{D}}^{\mathrm{b}}(R_n) \rangle$ of $s$, then $s$ is a nodal singularity, i.e.\ an $A_1$-singularity $\smash{\widehat{{\mathcal O}}_{X,s}} \cong \mathbb{C}\llbracket z_0, \ldots, z_{d} \rrbracket/(z_0^2 + \cdots + z_{d}^2 )$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.1
nodes.statement:
Let $X$ be an odd-dimensional projective Gorenstein variety over $\mathbb{C}$ such that $\operatorname{\mathsf{D}}^{\mathrm{b}}(X)$ admits a KSOD\xspace.\nopagebreak

  If $s \in \mathsf{Sing}(X)$ is an ADE-hypersurface singularity,
  then $s$ is already nodal, that is an $A_1$-singularity $\smash{\widehat{{\mathcal O}}_{X,s}} \cong \mathbb{C}\llbracket z_0, \ldots, z_{d}\rrbracket/(z_0^2 + \cdots + z_{d}^2 )$ with $d = \mathsf{dim} X$.

nodes.name: Claim 2.1
nodes.statement: If $\operatorname{\mathsf{D}}^{\mathrm{b}}(X)$ admits a tilting object, then $s$ is nodal (i.e.\ an $A_1$-singularity).

nodes.name: Theorem 1.15: Cf also
nodes.statement:
Let $S = \mathbb{C}\llbracket z_0, \ldots, z_d \rrbracket/(f)$ be a complete local $d$-dimensional ADE-hypersurface singularity or $S \in \mathfrak{S}$. 
  
  If $d$ is odd and there is a $\mathbb{C}$-linear triangle equivalence $\operatorname{\mathsf{D}}^{\mathrm{sg}}(S) \cong \operatorname{\mathsf{D}}^{\mathrm{sg}}(R)$
  for a finite-dimensional Gorenstein $\mathbb{C}$-algebra $R$, then $S$ is nodal, i.e.\ an $A_1$-singularity $S \cong \mathbb{C}\llbracket z_0, \ldots, z_d \rrbracket/(z_0^2 + \cdots + z_d^2 )$.

nodes.name: Theorem 2.13
nodes.statement:
Let $S \cong \mathbb{C}\llbracket z_1, \ldots, z_n \rrbracket/I$ be a $3$-dimensional Gorenstein $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with an isolated singularity and assume that $\mathsf{Spec} S$ has a small resolution.\nopagebreak

   Then $\operatorname{\mathsf{D}}^{\mathrm{sg}}(S)$ contains a cluster-tilting object. Moreover, if the quiver of every cluster-tilting object in $\operatorname{\mathsf{D}}^{\mathrm{sg}}(S)$ contains no loops 
   or $2$-cycles, then $S$ is an $A_1$-singularity.
